title: No Verified Case Can Excuse Vietnam’s Dog-Trade Gaps
excerpt: Stolen-pet claims and rabies risks demand records, quarantine, and accountability—not slogans. Vietnam needs transparent reform and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A family losing a dog to theft faces real grief. But public advocacy must not turn an unverified raid, conviction, poison-bait case, or shipment into fact. No specific incident, court judgment, police seizure, or government dataset is available here to prove those claims. That gap does not defend the trade. It shows why transparent records and enforceable protection matter.

Tradition cannot replace proof

“Farm-raised” claims require traceability: registered premises, movement records, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and humane handling. Without those records, buyers and authorities cannot reliably distinguish lawful activity from stolen companion animals, illegally transported dogs, or animals moved around quarantine controls. Claims about universal theft or nonexistent farms need case files and inspection data, not repetition.

Biosecurity has no shortcut

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. World Health Organization rabies guidance does not establish properly cooked meat as a rabies transmission route.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply-chain failures are parallel biosecurity concerns, not automatically one causal chain. Both demand competent veterinary controls, humane enforcement, and public reporting. Vietnamese families, rescuers, veterinarians, and local reformers deserve systems that protect companions and communities from theft, cruelty, and disease risk.

Demand records. Demand abolition.

Official public-health targets and SDE’s campaign demand are distinct. SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.

facebook_post:
A stolen dog is not a slogan. It is a family loss—and every claim about theft, transport, or slaughter must stand on verifiable police, court, veterinary, or inspection records.

No specific incident is documented here strongly enough to support dramatic raid or conviction claims. That does not make the trade safe. It makes transparent oversight urgent. “Farm-raised” claims need traceability, registered premises, movement records, veterinary inspection, and quarantine compliance. Without those safeguards, buyers cannot know whether animals entered supply chains lawfully or through theft and illegal transport.

Rabies control also requires precision. Infection risk comes from infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route.

Vietnamese families, veterinarians, rescuers, and local leaders can demand better: records, enforcement, companion-animal protection, and complete abolition by 2030.
